## Natural history notes

A tiny oak gall wasp characterized less by the adult insect than by the distinctive leafy, rosette-like galls it induces on live oaks. In Florida, the Leafy Oak Gall Wasp is associated with live oak and sand live oak, especially in oak hammocks, scrubby oak habitats, yards, parks, and forest edges where these trees occur. The larva develops inside the gall, which is made from the oak’s own tissue and provides food and shelter; these galls are usually more visually striking than harmful and also support parasitoids and other gall-associated insects.
